task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and an explainer of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the proposed school attendance-zone changes in Merrowfield and what they would mean for families. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Merrowfield School Board has published a proposed attendance-zone map for new enrollments in the 2027-28 school year.
The map is a proposal for public comment, not an adopted assignment notice for individual children.
Under the proposal, currently enrolled pupils could remain at their present schools; the draft does not require every household in a changed block to move schools.
The proposed treatment of younger siblings has not been settled and is listed as a question for consultation.
North Meadow School has 398 pupils against a planning capacity of 360, while nearby River Step School has 332 pupils against a planning capacity of 400.
The district says whole-school totals do not show every year group's available places or the suitability of particular rooms.
The draft shifts several future-enrollment blocks toward River Step while considering walking routes and the river's limited crossing points.
A short distance on the map can involve a longer walk when a household must reach the nearest bridge.
Planning officer Dena Orr said, "We are drawing a route to a school, not just a line around a number of houses."
The district will accept comments identifying route barriers, anticipated housing changes and family implications not represented in the draft data.
Comments will inform a revised proposal for the board rather than act as a household referendum on each boundary segment.
Parent group representative Lora Senn said, "Please answer the sibling question before asking families to treat the map as a settled plan."
The district has scheduled public sessions at both schools and will accept written comments from people unable to attend.
The draft boundary document contains no final transport entitlement for a particular address.
Any revised transport arrangements will be published with the final adopted enrollment policy rather than inferred from the draft map.
The planning capacities reflect the district's current room-use assumptions and are not a guarantee that every spare place fits every year group.
The district has not proposed closing either school or selling either site.
One housing development included in the projections has planning approval but no confirmed occupancy schedule.
The district will revise its projected pupil totals if the development timetable changes before adoption.
Older printed maps show the former footbridge, which is no longer part of the designated school walking route.
The board has not recorded its final vote on the proposal or announced implementation instructions for current pupils.
The supplied figures concern these schools and this planning exercise, not a citywide measure of educational quality.

forbidden_additions: An adopted map, compulsory transfers for all current pupils or a settled sibling policy.
Guaranteed transport from a particular address or a planned school closure.
School quality inferred from enrollment or building capacity.
preserve: The proposal's future-enrollment scope and unresolved family questions.
Geographic routes and year-group capacity rather than simple whole-school arithmetic alone.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
